title: Evaluation of previous-snapshot sources
statement: Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine, let $\ell$ be a list of bit sources, and let $T$ be a natural number. For binary input $x$, a list of Boolean blocks, a word $w$, and natural numbers $i,t$, suppose every block at index $i'<i$ equals the configuration-expansion block at index $i'$, and the snapshot index for time $t$ is less than $i$. Then evaluating, on $x$ and the given blocks, the list of sources for the snapshot immediately preceding time $t+1$ yields the encoding of the snapshot of $M$ on $w$ at time $t$.
